transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

To be honest, lately I feel like how I see myself depends almost completely on what I weigh or how my body looks. It’s just really starting to affect how I feel about myself every day, and my wife encouraged me to come in and talk to someone about it.
Do you currently have, or have you had in the past, any episodes of binge eating, where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel like you can't stop?

Yes, especially late at night when everyone is asleep; I'll stand at the counter eating leftovers, cereal, or peanut butter, consuming way more than a normal dinner. Once I start, it feels like a switch flips and I just keep shoveling food in even when a part of me is telling me to stop, until I'm uncomfortably full.
After these episodes of binge eating, do you ever try to compensate by doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or excessively exercising to get rid of the calories you consumed?

It's really hard to admit, but on the worst nights I make myself throw up in the bathroom with the shower running so my family won't hear. On other days, I try to "reset" by living on just coffee and an apple, or forcing myself to go on long, punishing walks after my late shifts even when I'm completely exhausted.
Can you estimate how often you engage in these compensatory behaviors, such as vomiting or extreme dieting and exercising, after binge eating episodes?

It's become almost a routine where it happens about once or twice a week. After one of those late-night blowout eating episodes, I'll either starve myself the next day or force myself to throw up to try and undo it.

Have you experienced any significant weight fluctuations over the past few months, and do these binge eating and compensatory behaviors interfere with your daily life, such as affecting your relationships, work, or social activities?

My weight hasn't shifted drastically, but even a couple of pounds makes me panic, and family members have started commenting on small changes. It definitely interferes with my life; on the days after, I'm so physically drained and preoccupied that I move slower at my register, avoid coworkers, and skip family meals, which my wife has really noticed.

Can you tell me more about how often you have these binge eating episodes without the compensatory behaviors, versus how often you have them followed by behaviors like vomiting or extreme dieting and exercising?

It's almost never without those behaviors; the panic and guilt are just too strong to ignore. Nearly every time I have one of those late-night blowout episodes, I feel compelled to do something to make up for it, whether that means starving myself the next day, forcing a punishing walk, or making myself throw up.
Can you clarify if there are times when you binge eat without subsequently engaging in compensatory behaviors like vomiting, extreme dieting, or excessive exercise, and if so, how often that occurs?

Honestly, it almost never happens that I just binge and do nothing to make up for it. The panic and guilt are so overwhelming that I always end up either restricting my food the next day, forcing a long walk, or making myself throw up. I really can't recall a time lately where I just let it go without trying to undo it.

Can you confirm if you have engaged in these compensatory behaviors, such as vomiting, extreme dieting, or excessive exercise, at least once a week for the past three months, as this could help clarify your condition?

Yes, I can confirm that—it's been happening at least once or twice a week, where I'll starve myself, throw up, or force those exhausting walks. It’s actually been going on for longer than three months, probably closer to six months now, ever since the chaos ramped up after our second baby was born.
